title: A paired phone stop speaks a code and address the screen does not show
body:
## Summary
landingView's spoken line for the phone stop always read the pairing address and code, also on a paired desk that draws no code.

## Description
desk/src/landing/model.ts:200 built `say` for the phone stop from the postcard's address and pin whatever `phone.paired` said. A paired desk draws no code (tools/tv-landing-test.cjs paper 1 pins "a paired phone shows no code") and its caption is "Select to pair another phone, or to forget them all." (desk/src/landing/model.ts:175). model.ts:188-191 promises the spoken line uses "the same words the eye reads, and nothing more". Registry: accessibility / name-and-description-wiring (the accessible text is the visible text). Fixed: paired, `say` is the caption head and sub; unpaired is unchanged.

## Flow
- Pair a phone, press Up from an app (desk/src/tv/keys.ts:387) so the lamp is on the phone
- the live region (desk-announce) reads "Phone paired. Open 10.0.0.7:3000/phone, then enter 4 7 1 1."
- fix: sayOf branches on phone.paired; TL-3 test pins both paired lines

## Expected impact
A screen-reader user on a paired desk hears what Select does instead of a code that is not on screen. Nothing else reads say.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the spoken line matches the drawn one
Before: 2 of 2 paired phone-stop cases spoke an unseen code ("Phone paired. Open 10.0.0.7:3000/phone, then enter 4 7 1 1."); tv-landing-test TL-3 red
After: 0 of 2: "Phone paired. Select to pair another phone, or to forget them all." / "No phone here. ..."; TL-3 green
Method: gate - red-then-green assertion in tools/tv-landing-test.cjs TL-3
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/landing/model.ts:200 (before) if (v.at === "phone") return parts([v.caption.head, `Open ${v.phone.url}, then enter ...`]);
red: actual 'Phone paired. Open 10.0.0.7:3000/phone, then enter 4 7 1 1.'

title: The lamp on a paired phone stop was drawn on nothing
body:
## Summary
Since TL-3 the phone is a stop paired or not, but only the unpaired postcard carried data-focused and a ring; on a paired desk the lamp on the phone lit nothing in either look.

## Description
desk/src/tv/landingRows.ts:48 lists "phone" as a stop always and desk/src/tv/keys.ts:387 sends Up from any app to it. desk/src/landing/themes/paper/Paper.tsx:196 drew the paired chip with data-role="desk-phone" and no data-focused, and desk/src/design/desk-landing.css had no focused rule for .pp-ph (only .pp-postcard[data-focused]); desk/src/landing/themes/blueprint/Blueprint.tsx:319 the same. Registry: accessibility / keyboard-navigation-models ("focus must always be somewhere visible"). Fixed in both looks: data-focused on the paired chip/plate while the lamp is on it, and the ring the postcard and Someone else wear.

## Flow
- paired desk, Up from Math Buddy: focus 5 = phone
- Before: caption changes to "Phone paired", no object lit
- fix: data-focused on the paired chip + .pp-ph[data-focused] ring (paper), .tc[data-focused] ring (blueprint)

## Expected impact
The learner sees where the lamp is on every stop of a paired desk. Could break: the ring's size at the badge (top right); capture owed.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every stop shows the lamp
Before: paper 0 of 1 and blueprint 0 of 1 paired phone hooks lit with the lamp on it; tv-landing-test TL-3 red
After: 1 of 1 in both looks, only while the lamp is on it; TL-3 green
Method: gate - render test in tools/tv-landing-test.cjs TL-3, red before the fix
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
red: actual '<div class="pp-ph" data-role="desk-phone" data-paired="true">' expected /data-focused="true"/
desk/src/design/desk-landing.css:139 .pp .pp-ph {...} (no focused rule before)

title: The hand-off said "Someone else" at a desk with no one seated
body:
## Summary
Both looks hard-coded the hand-off word for the second action as "Someone else", while the shelf reads "Choose who" when no one is seated, and an app Selected at that desk hands off to it.

## Description
desk/src/landing/model.ts:297 sets place to "Choose who" with no learner; desk/src/landing/LandingTV.tsx:30 maps an app Selected before anyone sat down to the "place" hand-off. desk/src/landing/themes/paper/Paper.tsx:220 named that hand-off "Someone else" and desk/src/landing/themes/blueprint/Blueprint.tsx:132 (ZOOM_WORD) the same: two hand-coded copies of the stop words, against desk/src/landing/themes/types.ts:3 "a theme ... decides no words". Fixed: model.ts handoffName(view, stop) is the one source; both looks read it.

## Flow
- nobody seated: Left, Select on an app (tools/tv-landing-live.cjs:177 drives this)
- Before: the flood names "Someone else" over a desk whose card said "Choose who"
- fix: handoffName -> view.place; Paper Zoom and Blueprint launch word read it

## Expected impact
A first desk with no one at it no longer flashes a word that implies someone is there. Nothing else changes; "Someone else" stays with someone seated.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for the hand-off words
Before: 2 of 2 looks said "Someone else" at an empty desk; 2 hand-coded copies; tv-landing-test paper 1 red
After: 2 of 2 say "Choose who"; 1 source (handoffName), 0 copies in the themes; green
Method: gate - render test of both looks' hand-off block, red before the fix
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/Paper.tsx:220 (before) const name = app ? app.name : stop === "place" ? "Someone else" : "Pair a phone";
desk/src/landing/themes/blueprint/Blueprint.tsx:132 (before) const ZOOM_WORD = { app: "Opening", place: "Someone else", phone: "Pair a phone" }

Before: 1 of 2 looks drew the view-model's empty caption (lock 1 red)
After: 2 of 2; 0 caption sentences written in a theme

Result: better

title: A still asked again mid-bake was baked a second time for no one
body:
## Summary
Every lamp move remounts both world sets, so each Still asks for its bitmap again; an ask for the still whose bake was in flight queued a second bake of the same bitmap.

## Description
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/Paper.tsx:288-294 key the WorldSets by seq, so every move remounts every Still (desk/src/landing/themes/paper/stills/Still.tsx:144 asks again). request() skipped an id only while it was in `queue`; pump() had already shifted the in-flight one (its idle wait of up to 1.5 s, then render, serialise, decode), so it was unshifted and baked again after the first finished, with every asker already answered. Registry: adaptive-fidelity-tiers / probe-deferral-to-idle (idle work must not repeat itself). Fixed: the in-flight id is named (inflight) and an ask for it joins the bake.

## Flow
- page load: 15 stills warm one per idle slot
- a lamp move while one is in flight remounts its Still, which asks again
- Before: the same still is baked twice; fix: requestStill skips the inflight id

## Expected impact
The first lamp moves after a load stop paying an extra off-screen render, serialise and image decode (main thread) per remount during warm-up. Could break: nothing waits on the second bake (its waiters list was empty).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one bake per bitmap
Before: one still asked twice while in flight: 2 bakes (landing-stills-test red "baked 2 times")
After: 1 bake, both askers answered (green)
Method: gate - queue test with a stubbed idle callback and a counting createElementNS
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/stills/Still.tsx:125 (before) if (!queue.includes(id)) { queue.unshift(id); pump(); }
red: the still was baked 2 times for one bitmap

title: A still that failed to bake left no trace in the perf kit's stats
body:
## Summary
Still.tsx swallowed every bake failure, and stillStats() (window.__ppStills) listed only declared and baked ids, so a failed still read like one still queued.

## Description
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/stills/Still.tsx:114 was `bake(id).catch(() => { /* stays live */ })`; stillStats (Still.tsx:36) is what tools/stick-perf/pass3.sh records per hold. A hold measured on a live layer could not tell a failed bake from a slow one. Fixed: stillStats().failed = [{ id, n, error }], cleared on a later successful bake; the still still renders live and retries on its next mount.

## Flow
- a bake throws (no DOM, an SVG decode error, a lost context)
- Before: nothing records it
- fix: the rejection is kept in `failed` and reported by stillStats

## Expected impact
The operator's stick holds can say which still stayed live and why. Behaviour on screen is unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failure leaves a record
Before: a bake that throws: 0 traces (stillStats().failed undefined; landing-stills-test red)
After: failed: [{ id, n: 1, error: "no DOM here" }] (green)
Method: gate - the queue test asserts the record, red before the fix
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
red: a failed bake is on the record: undefined
tools/stick-perf/pass3.sh records window.__ppStills()

title: No node test walked the stops the D-pad has
body:
## Summary
The suite asserted one lit stop (Math Buddy, paper); the stop list is landingStops() and nothing derived the focus checks from it, which is how the paired phone stop went unlit.

## Description
tools/tv-landing-test.cjs paper 1 asserted data-focused on maths only; the live walk (tools/tv-landing-live.cjs) cannot run in a gate. A new test takes the stops from desk/src/tv/landingRows.ts landingStops for each scenario desk and the looks from THEMES, and asserts each stop lights at least one element and only its own.

## Flow
- for each scenario desk, each stop index, each look: render with focus at that index
- assert >= 1 data-focused="true" and every lit element is that stop
- seed: remove the paired chip's data-focused -> red; restore -> green

## Expected impact
A stop added later (or a look) cannot ship unlit. Pure test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the focus check derives from the ground truth
Before: 1 of 46 stop x look x desk cases asserted lit
After: 46 of 46; seeded red on the phone chip
Method: gate - new test, seeded violation red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
seed red: paper/returning: the lamp on phone is drawn on nothing
tools/tv-landing-test.cjs "every stop the D-pad walks is drawn lit in every look"

body:

title: Writing's world still rasters its sky and front hill live on every lamp move
body:
## Summary
Pass 3 made every world's sky, hills and front into stills except the empty world, which Writing (a stop on every desk with Essay Master since ad847bdf) shows.

## Description
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/worlds.tsx:320-326 emptyWorld: the hills reuse the Math Buddy stills, but the sky (a 2840 x 1320 gradient rect) and the front hill are live SVG, so the move into and out of Writing rasters them tile by tile, the cost pass 3 removed elsewhere (docs/concepts/STICK-PERFORMANCE-2026-10-21.md, Pass 3: lamp move 641-669 -> 271-283 ms). The empty sky paints the same gradient as the .pp-sky backdrop under it (worlds.tsx:35, Paper.tsx:284), so it may be droppable rather than baked. Stills budget: the 40 MB ceiling in tools/landing-stills-test.cjs (measured 36.9 MB) leaves about 3 MB.

## Flow
- measure a lamp move essay -> writing on the stick (pass3.sh, 1.2 s window)
- B arm: drop the empty sky layer (backdrop shows the same gradient) and make the front a still
- same window, plus a look PSNR of the Writing landing

## Expected impact
The fourth stop moves like the other three. Could break: the empty world's look under the unpaired host scale (the backdrop is not scaled).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - the Writing move without tile raster
Before: emptyWorld: 2 of 4 layers live, incl. the 2840 x 1320 sky (worlds.tsx:322, :325)
After: predicted 0 of 4 live; not measured
Method: simulation - three cases walked (essay -> writing, writing -> essay, an empty profile); the stick window is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/worlds.tsx:322 L(0.1, "sky", true, <><defs><SkyGradient id="mSky" .../><SkyRect id="mSky" /></>)
:325 L(1.25, "hero", false, <Hill base={940} .../>)
instrument: tools/stick-perf/pass3.sh lamp essay->writing, longest gap in the 1.2 s window, both arms; look PSNR >= 45 dB; landing-stills-test 40 MB ceiling green

title: Every declared still is baked for every desk, worlds not on the profile included
body:
## Summary
warmAll() queues all 15 declared stills once any still mounts, so a desk without Math Buddy still holds its sky and front bitmaps resident.

## Description
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/stills/Still.tsx:140-143 warmAll bakes every id in `declared`, which worlds.tsx fills at module load for all three worlds. Pass 3 measured the bitmaps at 36.9 MB and +46 MB GL mtrack inside a module because they stay resident (docs/concepts/STICK-PERFORMANCE-2026-10-21.md). On a desk like Jakub's (english, essay) maths-sky and maths-front (about 6 MB) can never be shown (the empty world uses only the maths hills).

## Flow
- pass the desk's apps to the stills (or warm on first request per world)
- bake only the stills of worlds on the desk plus the empty world's
- compare __ppStills bytes and GL mtrack in a module on a two-app desk

## Expected impact
Less resident GPU memory on desks with fewer apps, on a stick with an 80 MB soft tile budget. Could break: a profile edit that adds an app then bakes on first move.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - GPU memory proportional to the desk
Before: 15 of 15 stills baked on any desk (36.9 MB measured on the three-app desk)
After: predicted 13 of 15 on a two-app desk without Math Buddy, about 6 MB less; not measured
Method: simulation - two desks walked from tools/tv-landing-test.cjs scenarios (returning, someoneElse)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/landing/themes/paper/stills/Still.tsx:142 for (const id of declared.keys()) if (!baked.has(id) && !queue.includes(id)) queue.push(id);
instrument: window.__ppStills().bytes and dumpsys meminfo GL mtrack inside a module, Jakub's desk, both arms (pass3.sh mem)

title: The locked blueprint look's faces are preloaded on every TV page load
body:
## Summary
Blueprint's next/font faces are preloaded on /tv although nothing can draw the look; its fonts.ts comment says a look never drawn never asks for them.

## Description
desk/src/landing/themes/index.ts:17 imports BLUEPRINT statically (its own note says the code ships). next/font preloads every face in the route's graph by default: the main checkout's production build (desk/.next/server/next-font-manifest.json, built 2026-10-21 17:22) lists 34 preloaded files for app/tv/page, of which Jost (2 files, 43.8 KB), IBM Plex Sans (2, 66.1 KB) and IBM Plex Mono 500 (2, 18.9 KB) come from desk/src/landing/themes/blueprint/fonts.ts. The comment at blueprint/fonts.ts:4 ("a look that is never drawn never asks for them") is false for preload. Fix: `preload: false` on the three blueprint faces (the look stays renderable in tests).

## Flow
- add preload: false to Jost, IBM_Plex_Sans, IBM_Plex_Mono in blueprint/fonts.ts
- next build
- count next-font-manifest app[/tv/page]

## Expected impact
The stick downloads about 129 KB fewer fonts on a cold load and the needed faces are not queued behind them. Could break: nothing draws blueprint.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer preloaded fonts on /tv
Before: 34 preloaded font files on /tv, 6 of them blueprint-only (128.8 KB), from the 17:22 build
After: predicted 28; needs a build to measure
Method: probe - Before read from the build manifest; After needs next build (Google font fetch, barred offline)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
next-font-manifest app["[project]/src/app/tv/page"]: 34 files; Jost 500 x2 (17204+26588), IBM Plex Sans 600 x2 (25868+40240), IBM Plex Mono 500 x2 (8848+10060)
desk/src/landing/themes/blueprint/fonts.ts:4
instrument: next build in desk/, then count next-font-manifest.json app["[project]/src/app/tv/page"]: 34 -> 28

title: Two Fraunces configurations are preloaded on /tv, one for the landing, one for Math Buddy
body:
## Summary
The landing loads Fraunces (opsz) and Math Buddy loads Fraunces (opsz + SOFT, normal + italic); /tv preloads 6 Fraunces files, 632 KB.

## Description
desk/src/landing/fonts.ts:11 Fraunces({ axes: ["opsz"] }) and desk/src/maths/fonts.ts:11-14 Fraunces({ axes: ["opsz", "SOFT"], style: ["normal", "italic"] }) are separate faces with separate files. Both are in the /tv graph (Paper.tsx and tv/screens.tsx). The landing could use Math Buddy's normal face (a superset of its axes) through one shared module, dropping its own pair. maths/fonts.ts is outside this context.

## Flow

- landing CSS keeps --pp-serif from it
- next build, count the manifest; look check on the landing title

## Expected impact
About two font files fewer on a cold /tv load. Could break: the landing title's look if the SOFT axis default differs.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one serif family config on /tv
Before: 6 Fraunces files preloaded on /tv (632,372 bytes), two configurations
After: predicted 4 files; not measured
Method: probe - Before from the 17:22 build manifest; After needs a build
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
next-font-manifest /tv: Fraunces x6 = 632372 bytes
desk/src/landing/fonts.ts:11; desk/src/maths/fonts.ts:11

title: The paired-phone badge draws a live phone when none is connected
body:
## Summary
The landing badge draws the paired glyph with its waves and says "Phone paired" from `joined`, while the caption on the same stop says "No phone here" from phonesLive.

## Description
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/Paper.tsx:196 draws PhoneGlyph paired and the hidden word "Phone paired" whenever view.phone.paired (= s.joined, desk/src/landing/model.ts:295). desk/src/landing/model.ts:175 says "No phone here" when phonesLive is 0. Joined-and-present and joined-and-absent render the same badge. The paired design rule (docs/concepts/TV-LED-PAIRED-EXPERIENCE-DESIGN-2026-10-19.md D1: "The TV reads presence, not history") and the stick walk's F3 (docs/concepts/STICK-DEADLINE-WALK-2026-10-21.md:78) name the same disagreement on other screens.

## Flow
- phone paired, its page closed: phonesLive 0
- landing: badge shows waves and "Phone paired"; lamp on the phone: caption "No phone here"
- fix: view.phone.live; the badge draws present vs absent (look decision on the absent glyph)

## Expected impact
The learner sees whether a phone is actually there before Selecting an app that hands work to it. Could break: the badge look; capture owed.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the badge tells present from absent
Before: 2 states (phonesLive 0 / >0, joined) -> 1 badge rendering
After: predicted 2 renderings; not built
Method: simulation - the walk's F3 case and two desks from tools/tv-landing-test.cjs TL-3
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/Paper.tsx:196 {view.phone.paired &&
Phone paired desk/src/landing/model.ts:175 s.phonesLive > 0 ? "Phone paired" : "No phone here"

title: A canvas with no 2D context bakes a blank bitmap over the live layer
body:
## Summary
paint() returns quietly when getContext("2d") is null, so bake() records a blank canvas as baked and the Still swaps its live hills for it.

## Description
desk/src/landing/themes/paper/stills/Still.tsx:104-110 paint: `const x = canvas.getContext("2d"); if (!x) return;` then bake stores the canvas in `baked` (Still.tsx:99). The Still component then renders the foreignObject with that empty canvas instead of the live drawing. A null context is rare (the context cannot be created), but the result is a missing sky or hill with no trace. Fix: paint throws, so the still stays live and lands in stillStats().failed.

## Flow
- getContext("2d") returns null on the stick
- Before: a blank bitmap replaces the live layer; after: the layer stays live and the failure is recorded
- test needs an Image/canvas stub around paint

## Expected impact
A failed bitmap can no longer blank a world layer. Could break: nothing when a context exists.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed paint keeps the live layer
Before: null context: 1 blank bitmap marked baked (code read, Still.tsx:106)
After: predicted: 0 baked, 1 failed record; not built (paint is not exported and the queue test has no canvas stub)
Method: simulation - the null-context path walked; the gate needs a canvas/Image stub
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a landing-stills-test case with stubbed Blob/URL/Image and a canvas whose getContext returns null: baked before, failed after

title: The hand-off shows a 20 px "Stylised" label that says nothing to the learner
body:
## Summary Every Select hand-off draws a diamond and the word "Stylised" at 20 px over "Opening ": a contest-mock label under On Air's 28 px floor that carries no meaning. ## Description desk/src/landing/themes/paper/Paper.tsx:231
Stylised
, styled at 20 px uppercase (desk/src/design/desk-landing.css:173). On Air (docs/DESIGN-ON-AIR.md) puts nothing under 28 px; the landing stylesheet's own exception (desk-landing.css:7-8) covers 20 px labels that never carry meaning alone, and this one carries none at all. Removing or rewording it changes the contest winner's ported look, so the owner decides. ## Flow - Select on any object: the flood, the emblem, "STYLISED", "Opening", the name - options: drop the label; or replace it with the stop's chip (e.g. "Marked") at >= 28 px ## Expected impact One less meaningless word on every hand-off. Could break: the hand-off's composition (owner's look check). ## Evaluation Claim: user - every word on the TV says something Before: 1 label of 0 meaning in the hand-off, at 20 px After: owner's choice Method: simulation - the hand-off walked for an app, the place card and the phone; the benefit is a look call Result: unmeasurable Gate: direction
